Two of the module axioms need more than $F$-bilinearity: \begin{itemize} \item $c = 1$: note that $c = 1 = \mfb(\id,\id)^{-1}\mfa(\id,\id)^{-1}\,\cdot\,\Delta^{\mfc}_{\id, 1}$, hence \[ \begin{aligned} 1 \cdot [a\ox b] &= [\mfb(\id,\id)^{-1}\mfa(\id,\id)^{-1}\Delta^{\mfa}_{\id,1}a \ox \Delta^{\mfb}_{\id, 1}b] \\ &= [\Delta^{\mfa}_{\id,\mfa(\id,\id)^{-1}}a \ox \Delta^{\mfb}_{\id,\mfb(\id,\id)^{-1}}b] \\ &= [a\ox b]. \end{aligned} \] \item $c_{1}c_{2}\cdot [a \ox b] = c_{1}\cdot c_{2}\cdot [a\ox b]$: assume $c_{1} = k_{1}\cdot\Delta^{\mfc}_{\tau_{1}, 1}$ and $c_{2}=k_{2}\cdot\Delta^{\mfc}_{\tau_{2},1}$. Then $c_{1}c_{2} = k_{1}\tau_{1}\left(k_{2}\right)\cdot \Delta^{\mfc}_{\tau_{1}\tau_{2},\mfc(\tau_{1},\tau_{2})} = k_{1}\tau_{1}\left(k_{2}\right)\mfa(\tau_{1},\tau_{2})\mfb(\tau_{1},\tau_{2})\cdot \Delta^{\mfc}_{\tau_{1}\tau_{2},1}$. Therefore, the left hand side is equal to \[ \begin{aligned} & \left[\left(k_{1}\tau_{1}(k_{2})\mfa(\tau_{1},\tau_{2})\mfb(\tau_{1},\tau_{2})\cdot \Delta^{\mfa}_{\tau_{1}\tau_{2}, 1}\right)a \ox \Delta^{\mfb}_{\tau_{1}\tau_{2},1}b\right] \\ =& \left[ k_{1}\tau_{1}(k_{2})\mfa(\tau_{1},\tau_{2})\cdot \Delta^{\mfa}_{\tau_{1}\tau_{2},1} a \ox \mfb(\tau_{1},\tau_{2})\Delta^{\mfb}_{\tau_{1}\tau_{2}, 1}b \right]\\ =& \left[ \Delta^{\mfa}_{\tau_{1},k_{1}}\Delta^{\mfa}_{\tau_{2},k_{2}} a \ox \Delta^{\mfb}_{\tau_{1},1}\Delta^{\mfb}_{\tau_{2},1}b \right]; \end{aligned} \] and the right hand side is also equal to \[ \begin{aligned} &\left(k_{1}\cdot \Delta^{\mfc}_{\tau_{1}, 1}\right) \left[ k_{2}\cdot\Delta^{\mfa}_{\tau_{2},1}a \ox \Delta^{\mfb}_{\tau_{2}, 1} b \right] \\ =& \left[ \left(k_{1}\cdot \Delta^{\mfa}_{\tau_{1}, 1}\right)\left(k_{2}\cdot\Delta^{\mfa}_{\tau_{2}, 1}\right)a \ox \Delta^{\mfb}_{\tau_{1},1}\Delta^{\mfb}_{\tau_{2},1}b \right]\\ =&\left[ k_{1}\tau_{1}(k_{2})\cdot \Delta^{\mfa}_{\tau_{1}\tau_{2},\mfa(\tau_{1},\tau_{2})}a \ox \Delta^{\mfb}_{\tau_{1}, 1}\Delta^{\mfb}_{\tau_{2},1}b \right]\\ =&\left[ \left(k_{1}\cdot \Delta^{\mfa}_{\tau_{1}, 1}\right)\left(k_{2}\cdot\Delta^{\mfa}_{\tau_{2}, 1}\right)a \ox \Delta^{\mfb}_{\tau_{1},1}\Delta^{\mfb}_{\tau_{2},1}b \right]. \end{aligned} \] \end{itemize} Expanding everything out and checking on the basic elements, we see that for any $x \in \left(\cross_{\mfa}\ox_{F}\cross_{\mfb}\right)^{\opp}$, $y \in \cross_{\mfc}$ and $z \in M$, $x \cdot y \cdot z = y \cdot x \cdot z$. In another word, we gave $M$ a $\left(\cross_{\mfc}, \cross_{\mfa} \ox_{F} \cross_{\mfb}\right)$-bimodule structure.
nodes.statement_short: $M$ = $\cross_\mfa\otimes_F\cross_\mfb$ modulo $(ka)\otimes b-a\otimes(kb)$, a $(\cross_\mfc,\cross_\mfa\otimes_F\cross_\mfb)$-bimodule.

nodes.name: M is the tensor product over K
nodes.statement: $M$ is isomorphic to $\cross_{\mfa}\ox_{K}\cross_{\mfb}$ as $F$-modules.
nodes.label: lem:M-iso-tensor-over-K

nodes.name: Proof of M is the tensor product over K
nodes.statement: The map $M \to \cross_{\mfa}\ox_{K}\cross_{\mfb}$ is obtained by descending the obvious $F$-linear map $\cross_{\mfa}\ox_{F}\cross_{\mfb}\to\cross_{\mfa}\ox_{K}\cross_{\mfb}$. By universal property of tensor product, there is an additive group homomorphism $\cross_{\mfa}\ox_{K}\cross_{\mfb} \to M$ given by $a \ox b \mapsto [a\ox b]$, this map is in fact $F$-linear. The two maps are inverse to each other.
nodes.statement_short: Mutually inverse maps between $M$ and the tensor product over $K$.

nodes.name: Dimension of M
nodes.statement: The $F$-dimension of $M$ is equal to ${\left(\dim_{F}K\right)}^{3}$, consequently $M$ is a finitely generated $\cross_{\mfc}$-module.
nodes.label: cor:dim-finite-M

nodes.name: Proof of Dimension of M
nodes.statement: By~\cref{lem:M-iso-tensor-over-K}, the dimension of $M$ is equal to $\dim_{F}\cross_{\mfa}\ox_{K}\cross_{\mfb} = \dim_{K}\cross_{\mfa}\ox_{K}\cross_{\mfb}\dim_{F}K$. By~\cref{lem:cross-product-basis}, $\dim_{K}\cross_{\mfa} = \dim_{K}\cross_{\mfb} = \dim_{F}K$.
nodes.statement_short: Dimension count via the tensor product over $K$.

nodes.name: Simple module S and index set J for the product cross product
nodes.statement: By~\cref{lem:direct-sum-simple-mod}, there exists some simple $\cross_{\mfc}$-module $S$ such that $\cross_{\mfc}$ is isomorphic to $\bigoplus_{i\in J}S$ as $\cross_{\mfc}$-module for some indexing set $J$. If we give $S$ the $F$-module structure by pulling back the $\cross_{\mfc}$-module structure, by restricting scalars $\cross_{\mfc}$ is isomorphic to $\bigoplus_{i\in J} S$ as $F$-module as well. Since $\cross_{\mfc}$ is a finite dimensional $F$-vector space, $J$ must be finite as well. Note that $S$ must be a finite dimensional $F$-vector space, because $S$ is finitely generated as $\cross_{\mfc}$-module and $\cross_{\mfc}$ has finite $F$-dimension. The indexing set $J$ must be nonempty, otherwise $\cross_{\mfc}$ being isomorphic to $\bigoplus_{\emptyset} S$ is a trivial ring; but simple rings are non-trivial. Since $J$ is finite, direct sum over $J$ and direct product over $J$ agree. Recall~\cref{con:self-tensor-opp-iso-end} and~\cref{con:end-vec-iso-matrix}, for all non-zero $m \in\mathbb{N}$, we have \[ \End_{\cross_{\mfc}}\left(S^{m}\right) \cong \mat_{m}\left(\End_{\cross_{\mfc}}S\right) \] as $F$-algebras, hence \[ \cross_{\mfc}^{\opp} \cong \End_{\cross_{\mfc}}\cross_{\mfc}\cong \End_{\cross_{\mfc}}S^{|J|} \cong \mat_{|J|}\left(\End_{\cross_{\mfc}}S\right) \] as $F$-algebras. Finally \[ \cross_{\mfc}\cong \mat_{|J|}\left(\End_{\cross_{\mfc}}\left(S\right)^{\opp}\right) \] as $F$-algebras.
nodes.statement_short: Write $\cross_\mfc\cong S^{J}$ for a simple module $S$ with finite nonempty $J$, so $\cross_\mfc\cong\Mat_{|J|}(\End(S)^{op})$.

nodes.name: First dimension equation
nodes.statement: \[ \left(\dim_{F}K\right)^{2} = |J|^{2}\dim_{F}\End_{\cross_{\mfc}}S. \]
nodes.label: cor:dim-eq-1

nodes.name: Proof of First dimension equation
nodes.statement: They are both equal to $\dim_{F}\cross_{\mfc}$ by~\cref{con:cross-product-mul-iso}.
nodes.statement_short: Both equal $\dim_F\cross_\mfc$.

nodes.name: Second dimension equation
nodes.statement: \[ |J|\dim_{F}S = \left(\dim_{F}K\right)^{2} \]
nodes.label: cor:dim-eq-2

nodes.name: Proof of Second dimension equation
nodes.statement: They are all equal to $\dim_{F}\cross_{\mfc} = \dim_{F}S^{|J|}$ by~\cref{con:cross-product-mul-iso}.
nodes.statement_short: Both equal $\dim_F\cross_\mfc$.

nodes.name: M is a power of S
nodes.statement: There exists a $\cross_{\mfc}$-linear isomorphism between $M$ and $S^{|J|\dim_{F}K}$.
conclusions: There exists a $\cross_{\mfc}$-linear isomorphism between $M$ and $S^{|J|\dim_{F}K}$
nodes.label: lem:M-iso-simple-pow

nodes.name: Proof of M is a power of S
nodes.statement: By~\cref{lem:iso-of-dim-eq}, we only need to show that $\dim_{F}M = \dim_{F}S^{|J|\dim_{F}K}$. We already have $\dim_{F}M = \left(\dim_{F}K\right)^{3}$ by~\cref{cor:dim-finite-M}. We also have $\dim_{F}S^{|J|\dim_{F}K} = |J|\dim_{F}K\dim_{F}S = \dim_{F}K \left(|J|\dim_{F}S\right) = \dim_{F}K\left(\dim_{F}K\right)^{2}$ by~\cref{cor:dim-eq-2}.
nodes.statement_short: Equal $F$-dimensions give an isomorphism of modules.

nodes.name: Reduce to dimensions
nodes.statement: By~\cref{lem:iso-of-dim-eq}, we only need to show that $\dim_{F}M = \dim_{F}S^{|J|\dim_{F}K}$.
nodes.statement_short: Suffices to compare dimensions.

nodes.name: Dimension of M
nodes.statement: We already have $\dim_{F}M = \left(\dim_{F}K\right)^{3}$ by~\cref{cor:dim-finite-M}.
nodes.statement_short: From the corollary.

nodes.name: Dimension of the power of S
nodes.statement: We also have $\dim_{F}S^{|J|\dim_{F}K} = |J|\dim_{F}K\dim_{F}S = \dim_{F}K \left(|J|\dim_{F}S\right) = \dim_{F}K\left(\dim_{F}K\right)^{2}$ by~\cref{cor:dim-eq-2}.
nodes.statement_short: From the second dimension equation.

nodes.name: M is a power of S as vector spaces
nodes.statement: As $F$-vector spaces, $M \cong S^{|J|\dim_{F}K}$.
nodes.label: cor:M-iso-simple-pow

nodes.name: Proof of M is a power of S as vector spaces
nodes.statement: Restricting scalars on the $\cross_{\mfc}$-linear isomorphism in~\cref{lem:M-iso-simple-pow}
nodes.statement_short: Restrict scalars.

nodes.name: Endomorphisms of M as a matrix algebra
nodes.statement: As $F$-algebras, $\End_{\cross_{\mfc}}M \cong \mat_{|J|\dim_{F}K}(\End_{\cross_{\mfc}}S)$.
nodes.label: cor:end-M-iso-mat

nodes.name: Proof of Endomorphisms of M as a matrix algebra
nodes.statement: From~\cref{cor:M-iso-simple-pow}, we have $\End_{\cross_{\mfc}}M\cong \End_{\cross_{\mfc}}\left(S^{|J|\dim_{F}K}\right)$. By~\cref{con:end-vec-iso-matrix}, they are isomorphic to $\mat_{|J|\dim_{F}K}(\End_{\cross_{\mfc}}S)$.
nodes.statement_short: Endomorphisms of a power of $S$ are matrices.

nodes.name: Third dimension equation
nodes.statement: \[ \dim_{F}\End_{\cross_{\mfc}}M = {\left(\dim_{F}K\right)}^{4}. \]
nodes.label: cor:dim-eq-3

nodes.name: Proof of Third dimension equation
nodes.statement: \[ \begin{aligned} \dim_{F}\End_{\cross_{\mfc}M} &= \dim_{F}\mat_{|J|\dim_{F}K}(\End_{\cross_{\mfc}}S) \\ &= \dim_{F}\left(\End_{\cross_{\mfc}}S\ox_{F}\mat_{|J|\dim_{F}K}(F)\right)\\ &= |J|^{2}\left(\dim_{F}K\right)^{2}\dim_{F}\End_{\cross_{\mfc}}S\\ &= \left(\dim_{F}K\right)^{2}\left(|J|^{2}\dim_{F}\End_{\cross_{\mfc}}S\right) \\ &= \left(\dim_{F}K\right)^{2}\left(\dim_{F}K\right)^{2}, \end{aligned} \] where the last equality is by~\cref{cor:dim-eq-1}.
nodes.statement_short: Dimension calculation using the first dimension equation.

nodes.name: Cross product of a product cocycle is Brauer equivalent to the tensor product
nodes.statement: The cross product $\cross_{\mfc}$ and the tensor product $\cross_{\mfa}\ox_{F}\cross_{\mfb}$ are Brauer equivalent.
conclusions: The cross product $\cross_{\mfc}$ and the tensor product $\cross_{\mfa}\ox_{F}\cross_{\mfb}$ are Brauer equivalent
nodes.label: thm:cross-mul

nodes.name: Proof of Cross product of a product cocycle is Brauer equivalent to the tensor product
nodes.statement: We define an $F$-algebra homomorphism $\phi : \left(\cross_{\mfa}\ox_{F}\cross_{\mfb}\right)^{\opp} \to \End_{\cross_{\mfc}}M$ by $x \mapsto (x \cdot \bullet)$. By~\cref{cor:dim-eq-3}, both sides has $F$-dimension $\left(\dim_{F}K\right)^{4}$, therefore, $\phi$ is an $F$-algebra isomorphism by~\cref{cor:alghom-bijective-of-dim-eq}. Hence we have another $F$-algebra isomorphism by composing the isomorphism in~\cref{cor:end-M-iso-mat}: \[ \phi^{\opp}:\cross_{\mfa}\ox_{F}\cross_{\mfb}\cong \left(\End_{\cross_{\mfc}}M\right)^{\opp}\cong \mat_{|J|\dim_{F}K}\left(\left(\End_{\cross_{\mfc}}S\right)^{\opp}\right). \] In the meantime, by~\cref{con:cross-product-mul-iso}, we have $\cross_{\mfc}\cong\mat_{|J|}\left(\left(\End_{\cross_{\mfc}}S\right)\opp\right)$; hence $\mat_{\dim_{F}K}\left(\cross_{\mfc}\right)$ is isomorphic to $\cross_{\mfa}\ox_{F}\cross_{\mfb}$.
nodes.statement_short: The action map $(\cross_\mfa\otimes\cross_\mfb)^{op}\to\End M$ is an isomorphism by dimension; compare matrix algebras.

nodes.name: Action map
nodes.statement: We define an $F$-algebra homomorphism $\phi : \left(\cross_{\mfa}\ox_{F}\cross_{\mfb}\right)^{\opp} \to \End_{\cross_{\mfc}}M$ by $x \mapsto (x \cdot \bullet)$.
nodes.statement_short: Define the action map $\phi$.

nodes.name: Dimension
nodes.statement: By~\cref{cor:dim-eq-3}, both sides has $F$-dimension $\left(\dim_{F}K\right)^{4}$, therefore, $\phi$ is an $F$-algebra isomorphism by~\cref{cor:alghom-bijective-of-dim-eq}.
nodes.statement_short: $\phi$ is an isomorphism by dimension.

nodes.name: Matrix algebra
nodes.statement: Hence we have another $F$-algebra isomorphism by composing the isomorphism in~\cref{cor:end-M-iso-mat}: \[ \phi^{\opp}:\cross_{\mfa}\ox_{F}\cross_{\mfb}\cong \left(\End_{\cross_{\mfc}}M\right)^{\opp}\cong \mat_{|J|\dim_{F}K}\left(\left(\End_{\cross_{\mfc}}S\right)^{\opp}\right). \]
nodes.statement_short: Compose with the matrix description.

nodes.name: Compare
nodes.statement: In the meantime, by~\cref{con:cross-product-mul-iso}, we have $\cross_{\mfc}\cong\mat_{|J|}\left(\left(\End_{\cross_{\mfc}}S\right)\opp\right)$; hence $\mat_{\dim_{F}K}\left(\cross_{\mfc}\right)$ is isomorphic to $\cross_{\mfa}\ox_{F}\cross_{\mfb}$.
nodes.statement_short: Compare with $\cross_\mfc$.

nodes.name: Group isomorphism Br(K/F) = H^2(Gal(K/F), K*)
nodes.statement: For a finite dimensional Galois field extension $K/F$, the relative Brauer group $\br(K/F)$ is isomorphic to the second group cohomology $\HH^{2}\left(\gal(K/F),K^{\star}\right)$.
nodes.statement_short: For finite Galois $K/F$, $\Br(K/F)\cong H^2(\mathrm{Gal}(K/F),K^*)$.
assumptions: For a finite dimensional Galois field extension $K/F$
conclusions: the relative Brauer group $\br(K/F)$ is isomorphic to the second group cohomology $\HH^{2}\left(\gal(K/F),K^{\star}\right)$

nodes.name: Proof of Group isomorphism Br(K/F) = H^2(Gal(K/F), K*)
nodes.statement: In~\cref{cor:relative-br-2nd-coh-bij}, we have seen that $\HH^{2}$ and $\cross$ form a bijection, thus it is sufficient to check either one of them preserves multiplication. The function $\cross: \HH^{2}\left(\gal(K/F), K^{\star}\right)$ preserves multiplication: let $[\mfa], [\mfb]$ be two elements in $\HH^{2}\left(\gal(K/F), K^{\star}\right)$, by~\cref{thm:cross-mul}$, \cross(\mfa\mfb)$ is indeed Brauer equivalent to $\cross(\mfa)\ox_{F}\cross(\mfb)$ that is \[ \left[\cross_{\mfa}\right]_{\sim_{\br}}\left[\cross_{\mfb}\right]_{\sim_{\br}} = \left[\cross_{\mfa\mfb}\right]. \]
nodes.statement_short: A bijection that preserves multiplication; use the cross product multiplicativity.
